item.title: US pauses operation to reopen Strait of Hormuz
item.description: BBC World News Digest — Wednesday, May 06, 2026 at 06:00 PM Podcast Episode: US pauses operation to reopen Strait of Hormuz Good morning. We begin with a significant development from Washington: The United States has announced a pause in its operations aimed at helping ships navigate the Strait of Hormuz. President Trump confirmed the move, citing what he described as 'great progress' towards a peace agreement with Iran. This decision marks a notable shift in regional strategy, coming as Iran's Foreign Minister, Abbas Araghchi, holds crucial discussions in China, widely expected to focus on de-escalation in the Gulf. Shifting focus to Eastern Europe, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has fiercely condemned the latest wave of Russian attacks on the country. Zelensky’s statement follows reports of renewed shelling and missile strikes, intensifying the ongoing conflict. More on these stories as we get it.

item.title: Couples looking for surrogates still going to Ukraine
item.description: BBC World News Digest — Thursday, May 07, 2026 at 07:19 PM Podcast Episode: Couples looking for surrogates still going to Ukraine 1. Iran considering US proposal as Trump says war will be 'over quickly': Iran is reportedly considering a US peace proposal, with Pakistan mediating efforts to end the war. 2. Islamic State-linked women arrive home in Australia from Syria: A group of nine women and children with links to Islamic State have been repatriated to Australia from Syria. 3. Israel strikes Beirut for first time since Hezbollah ceasefire: Israel has conducted its first strike in Beirut since mid-April, targeting a senior Hezbollah figure. 4. Shell latest oil giant to see profits surge due to Iran war impact: Shell has reported a significant profit surge, benefiting from the volatility in oil prices linked to the Iran war. 5. DR Congo president hints at extending his term and delaying polls: DR Congo's president has indicated he may seek to extend his term beyond 2028 and delay elections. 6. Massive Alaska megatsunami was second largest ever recorded: New research indicates glacier melt from climate change is increasing the risk of megatsunamis, following a massive event in Alaska. 7. To stay or risk the 'Road of Death' - Ukrainian civilians trapped in frontline city: Civilians in the frontline Ukrainian city of Oleshky report being cut off from essential supplies for months, facing dire choices. 8. German police raid neo-Nazi criminal youth groups: German police have conducted widespread raids across 12 states targeting neo-Nazi criminal youth groups. 9. Russia ignores Ukraine's unilateral ceasefire and attacks kindergarten: Ukraine accuses Russia of spurning a unilateral ceasefire and attacking a kindergarten, prompting Kyiv to consider further action. 10. Trump's hopes for an Iran peace deal come with caveats: Despite signs of momentum for an Iran peace deal, President Trump has introduced caveats regarding the negotiations. 11. China calls for Strait to be reopened 'as soon as possible' in Iran talks: During talks with Iran's foreign minister, China has called for the Strait to be reopened "as soon as possible". 12. Russian attacks kill more than 20 ahead of rival ceasefires proposed by Kyiv and Moscow: Over 20 people have been killed by Russian attacks ahead of rival ceasefire proposals from Kyiv and Moscow. 13. What is Trump's 'Project Freedom' in the Strait of Hormuz?: President Trump has paused "Project Freedom," a US military operation in the Strait of Hormuz announced earlier this week. 14. Romanian PM ousted in no-confidence vote: The Romanian Prime Minister has been ousted in a no-confidence vote, with coalition partners joining the opposition. 15. Ukraine is a global surrogacy hub - but that could be about to end: Ukraine is considering a law that could ban foreign access to surrogacy, potentially ending its status as a global hub. 16. Key bridge linking North Korea and Russia almost finished, satellite images show: Satellite images reveal a key bridge linking North Korea and Russia is nearing completion, signifying a deepening relationship between the two nations. 17. Gas tax: How beer fuelled a debate on Australia's energy giants: Australia is debating taxing gas exports, with campaigners arguing the country is giving away its gas 'for free' compared to other nations. 18. Robot wars - what an operation in Ukraine tells us about the battlefield of the near future: Ukraine's use of robots and drones to capture territory highlights the potential future of unmanned warfare on the battlefield.
